# [STORY] As a maintainer, I want the issue templates and audit tooling kept correct, so that every audit applies one fixed standard

## User Story
**As a** maintainer
**I want** the four issue templates and the audit tooling kept correct
**So that** every audit under this epic applies one fixed standard instead of a moving one

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the three templates that carry acceptance criteria, when a new
      issue is opened from one, then it must name the test or command that
      proves each criterion, and a date is stated not to be a proof
      (`grep -c 'not a proof' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{user-story,task,bug}.md`)
- [x] Given the templates, when they are read, then no section duplicates a
      GitHub feature: no child list, no `Parent: #N` line, no `## Sprint`
      (`grep -L '^## Sprint\|^## Child Stories\|^## Technical Tasks\|^Parent: #' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md`
      lists all four)
- [x] Given the templates, when they are read, then the label rule is stated:
      one type label, one priority label, `sprint-N` retired
      (`grep -c 'one type\|sprint-N' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md` returns 2 each)
- [x] Given the stories that carried `## Sprint`, when the template dropped
      it, then the section is gone from them too and cannot come back
      (`audit-check.py --all | grep '## Sprint'` prints nothing)
- [x] Given `.claude/skills/audit-artifacts/`, when an audit runs, then the
      skill and the writing standard match the templates they enforce
      (manual: read Gate 1 and steps 4-5 of `SKILL.md` against
      `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md`)

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Story Points
**Estimate:** 5

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Meets [Definition of Done](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md)

## Notes
This story is the standard the other 12 stories under #251 audit against. It
stays open for the life of the epic: a template or skill change found
mid-audit lands here, not in the story that happened to find it.

The epic template carries no acceptance-criteria section, so the first
criterion covers the three that do. That is also why Gate 4 does not apply
in the skill's Epic mode.

The fifth criterion is a manual read because the agreement is between prose
and prose. The mechanical half moved into `audit-check.py` instead: it now
reports `## Sprint` alongside the child lists, so a template section that
was retired cannot quietly return to an issue body.
